angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 480,659 km at 19.55 pc = 0.33 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 51.1573 +/- 0.0250 mas (same row, RUWE 0.99): 19.55 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.6909 +/- 0.0492 solar radii from Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2194 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract): 480,659 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.74 +/- 0.0854 solar masses from Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2194 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4756 +/- 50 K from Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2194 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2194 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2194.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.628, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
